subject: ventures/uk-holiday-pay-calculator
professional: a UK payroll specialist / employment-law HR adviser who checks starters', leavers', part-timers' and irregular-hours workers' statutory holiday and final-pay holiday under the Working Time Regulations 1998

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against the live GOV.UK 'Holiday entitlement' guide (fetched as JSON from www.gov.uk/api/content/holiday-entitlement-rights, 2026-11-26) with scratchpad checks.mjs/checks2.mjs. Pass: 5 days full year = 28; 6 days capped at 28; 3 days = 16.8 full-year days (GOV.UK example); leaver 1 Jan-30 Jun 2026, 5 days: 181/365*28 = 13.885 -> 14 days (GOV.UK half-year = 14), 9 left after 5 taken, 9 * 600/5 = GBP 1,080; worked example starter 14 Apr 2026: 262/365*28 = 20.099, rounded up 20.5, 17.5 left, GBP 2,100; year starting 2027-03-01 has 366 days. Fail: (1) GOV.UK's own irregular-hours example, 30 hours in a weekly pay period -> 4 hours of leave (12.07% = 3.621, 'must be rounded up to the nearest hour if ... 0.5 of an hour or more'); the tool gives 3.62 and has no pay-period input, so 52 weeks of 30 h gives 188.29 h where per-period accrual gives 208 h. (2) No date gate: GOV.UK says the 12.07% accrual and rolled-up pay apply only to leave years beginning on or after 1 April 2024; a leave year starting 2023-04-01 still gets the 12.07% result and the rolled-up pay finding. (3) Full-year 3-day worker is told '17 days of statutory holiday' where GOV.UK says 'at least 16.8'. (4) Rounding happens after r2(), so 35 part-year cases round down by under 0.005 day (0.5 day/week, 131 days: exact 1.00493, entitled 1). (5) Worked example's contract check reports '25-day contract is below statutory' with 8 bank holidays counted as leave entered alongside it. Arithmetic right, method gaps on the irregular-hours path: 2.
evidence.completeness: Walked in Chromium via Playwright (scratchpad walk.cjs, files served by route interception) at 375 px: no horizontal scroll; Load an example fills and computes (20.5 days, 17.5 left, GBP 2,100); pattern switch hides/shows the regular vs irregular fields; irregular 1000 h at GBP 12.50 with 40 taken -> 120.7 h accrued, 80.7 left; Clear then Work out shows the first validation error; Download result saves uk-holiday-pay.txt; usage counter records example_loaded and summary_downloaded in localStorage; opt-out button stores the flag and disables itself; LICENSE and the five sibling links load (200). No console errors. Every README/page feature (5.6 weeks, 28 cap, pro rata starters and leavers, 12.07%, days left, unused-day value, contract check, bank holidays) is present. No stubs or TODOs: 3.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject dir: tests 28, pass 28, fail 0 (0.18 s); the README's repo-root command also passes 28/28. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py (test command node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs, because the quoted glob without a shell ran no tests): roundUpHalf ceil -> round caught; cap > -> >= caught; leaver end date minus a day caught; rolled-up uplift *1.01 caught; contract check < -> <= SURVIVED; irregular 'leaving with unused hours' finding ungated from leave SURVIVED. Arithmetic is pinned; finding branches and the boundaries are not, and no test encodes a GOV.UK worked example for irregular hours: 3.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (146 lines), index.html script (lines 138-189), usage.mjs, all three test files. Pure engine, validated inputs with named errors, dates parsed strictly (rejects 2026-02-30), localStorage guarded, output escaped. Defects: roundUpHalf applies r2 before ceil (calc.mjs:18), so the 'never round down' promise breaks by up to 0.005 day; two money formatters, so findings say 'GBP 120' while the table says '£120' on the same screen (calc.mjs:16 vs index.html:145); very long one-line statements (calc.mjs:95, 142) are hard to review; bank holidays subtract from 'left to choose' (12.5) while 'Days remaining' says 17.5 for the same example with no explanation; footer list missing a comma (index.html:133). Acceptable: 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: 5.6 weeks / 28 cap / 16.8 for 3 days (GOV.UK Entitlement), pro rata for starters (GOV.UK 'pro-rata' alternative), 12.07% for leave years from 1 April 2024 and rolled-up pay only then (GOV.UK Holiday pay), 52 paid weeks average (GOV.UK Holiday pay), payment in lieu on leaving, deductions only if agreed in writing, nothing uploaded (page.test asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon; walk saw none), usage events named = events recorded, disclaimer in footer, README, header note and downloaded summary, served-copy reports no placeholder origin in llms.txt/sitemap. Unbacked or wrong: FAQ 'Employers should round up to the next half day' for a full-year part-timer (GOV.UK: 'at least 16.8 days') and the headline '17 days of statutory holiday'; the 12.07% FAQ states the April 2024 limit but the engine does not apply it; the worked example (the first thing a visitor sees) flags a 25-day contract as unlawful though 8 bank holidays are entered alongside it, the common '25 days plus bank holidays' contract; VENTURE.yaml says it competes with GOV.UK 'by adding the irregular-hours method', which GOV.UK's calculator already has: 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked as a 3-day part-timer, a 14 April starter and a 30 June leaver: each gets a defensible day count, days left and a final-pay figure in under a minute, with a 'get it in writing' and Acas step. A payroll specialist would hit in the first hour: irregular-hours workers on a pay-period basis (the main 12.07% population) get an unrounded annual total instead of per-period hours; pre-April-2024 leave years get the wrong method; no reg 15A monthly accrual for first-year starters (GOV.UK's default for a 13 January starter is 1/12 per month, 2.5 days for January); bank holidays not pro-rated for starters (the example's starter after 14 April 2026 sees 5 E&W bank holidays, not 8); holiday pay for irregular hours uses a single hourly rate rather than the 52-paid-week average. Usable for regular-hours checks: 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with GOV.UK 'Holiday entitlement' (Entitlement, Calculate leave entitlement, Holiday pay, Taking holiday before leaving) and WTR 1998 regs 13, 13A, 14, 15A, 15B, 16. Matches: 5.6 weeks capped at 28; part-time pro rata; leaver accrual on proportion of year with payment in lieu; 12.07% rate; rolled-up pay limited to irregular/part-year; 52 paid weeks reference; 3-months-less-a-day claim limit. Departs: reg 15B accrual is per pay period with rounding to the nearest hour at 0.5, not 12.07% of an annual total; no 1 April 2024 transition gate; full-year rounding presented as the statutory figure; reg 15A first-year monthly accrual not offered; no normal-vs-basic rate split for the 4 + 1.6 weeks. A payroll specialist would sign off the regular-hours path, not the irregular-hours one: 2.

mutations.change: irregular 'leaving with unused hours' finding: if (leave && remaining > 0) -> if (remaining > 0)

defects.what: Irregular-hours accrual is 12.07% of an annual hours total with no pay period: WTR reg 15B and GOV.UK accrue per pay period and round to the nearest hour at 0.5, so GOV.UK's own example (30 h in a weekly period = 4 h) comes out 3.62 h, and a year of 30-hour weeks is 188.29 h instead of 208 h

No 1 April 2024 gate: a leave year starting before 1 April 2024 still gets the 12.07% accrual and the rolled-up holiday pay finding, which GOV.UK says do not apply (rolled-up pay is not allowed) for those leave years; the FAQ states the limit but the engine ignores yearStart

The worked example flags a 25-day contract as below the statutory minimum while 8 bank holidays are entered as counting towards leave; the contract field does not say whether bank holidays are included, so the common '25 days plus bank holidays' contract (33 days) is reported unlawful

Full-year rounding is presented as the statutory figure: a 3-day worker is told '17 days of statutory holiday' and the FAQ says employers should round up, whereas GOV.UK says 'at least 16.8 days'; a worker could dispute a lawful 16.8
roundUpHalf rounds to 2 dp before ceil, so 35 part-year cases round down by under 0.005 day (0.5 day/week, 131 days: 1.00493 -> 1), against the page's 'Employers should not round down'

No reg 15A first-year monthly accrual (GOV.UK's 1/12 per month, 13 January starter = 2.5 days for January) and bank holidays are not limited to those in the employed period (the 14 April 2026 starter in the example sees 5 E&W bank holidays, not 8)
Two money formatters: findings and summary say 'GBP 120' while the table says '£120' on the same screen
Contract-check boundary and the irregular leaver finding are untested: contractShare < -> <= and dropping the leave gate both survive
VENTURE.yaml says it competes with the GOV.UK calculator 'by adding the irregular-hours method', which GOV.UK's calculator already offers

verdict: A small, private, honest-looking GB holiday calculator whose regular-hours path recomputes cleanly against GOV.UK (28-day cap, 16.8 days for 3 days, 30 June leaver 14 days and GBP 1,080, 14 April starter 20.5 days) and whose page works end to end in Chromium with 28 passing tests and 4 of 6 seeded mutants caught. It does not meet the bar: correctness, claims, fitness and domain are 2. The irregular-hours path, the one it markets as its edge, takes 12.07% of an annual total instead of per-pay-period accrual rounded to the hour (GOV.UK's 30-hour example is 4 h; the tool says 3.62), applies 12.07% and rolled-up pay to pre-April-2024 leave years, and the worked example tells a '25 days plus bank holidays' worker their contract is unlawful. Finished (completeness 3), not payroll-specialist grade until the reg 15B accrual and the 2024 transition gate are modelled.
